title: A CI workflow started by the candidate push is not handed the release's target, so binaries it builds stamp themselves dev
body:
## What happened

Intent 3.3.1's published Linux musl binaries report their source kind as `dev`, while its darwin binaries report `release`; both are built at the release commit c64a42e29. Intent's linux-release workflow builds them on GitHub CI when the cut pushes candidate/v3.3.1, before the tag exists. Intent stamps `release` only where a tag sits at the commit or `DEVBIN_RELEASE_TARGET_TAG` is set. A cut hands `DEVBIN_RELEASE_VERSION` and `DEVBIN_RELEASE_TARGET_TAG` only to the commands it runs itself (docs/configuration.md, issue 0327; lib/pages/release.md): preflight, derived, the gates and legs, the macOS stage, the formula step and after. A CI workflow started by the candidate push is handed neither. Found by agentic-engineering's devvm 0.5.0 arm64 rehearsal on 2026-11-13 and diagnosed by intent-vc.

## Why it matters

Any project whose CI builds release artefacts on the candidate branch cannot read the release's target the way the rest of the cut does, so each one works it out for itself in its own workflow (Intent's interim fix is config in its workflow). That is a per-project special case of something the core already owns.

## Options, none chosen

- Document a supported way for a candidate-triggered workflow to derive the pair from the tree (the version the tree declares and `release.tag`), eg a `bin/devbin release target` verb that prints both, so a workflow step exports them.
- Carry the pair in the candidate itself, eg a file or a ref the workflow reads.
- Leave it to each project's workflow, and say so in release.md.

## Resolution

cc, 2026-11-17 11:52Z by date -u: fixed by unit 0352-1, landed at ad3c9a12 for 0.1.27, from the stack 0354-1 then 0352-1 tested at 0647d816. Option 1, in the shape agreed with vc (decision 206). `bin/devbin release target [--ref <ref>]` prints the release's target as the tree declares it, `DEVBIN_RELEASE_VERSION=<version>` and `DEVBIN_RELEASE_TARGET_TAG=<tag>`, the lines a CI environment file takes, by release_tree_target (lib/release.steps), the one derivation, which gates_verb uses too. With `--ref`, the ref the run was started by, it prints them only for this release's candidate (release.publish.candidate filled with the tree's tag) or for that tag. Any other ref prints nothing and exits 0, saying so on stderr, and a candidate branch of another release's tag is refused, exit 1, naming both tags. It writes nothing, takes no lock and reads no history, which an arm proves in a shallow clone detached at the tag. A workflow's step is one line: `bin/devbin release target --ref "$GITHUB_REF" >>"$GITHUB_ENV"`. target joins release.verbs' default, so a project that declares release.verbs adds it to use the verb; Intent's adoption notice follows 0.1.27's sweep.

With it, on vc's word: release_tag_version (lib/helpers), the reading of a tag back to its version, which formula's tag_version now calls too (release_versions reads its own way, filed as 0371); and the tag row's readers gain gates, which gates_verb reads.

Arms: ten in releasecore.bats, each red at the base and green at the tip under BSD and GNU in the stack's first run (Desk slot 01M7MK7XB7TV226TJM041ZQCQF). There one existing arm, which pins release.verbs' default, went red for want of target. Amended, it and releasecore.bats whole were green under BSD and GNU, with test scans 61 of 61, in the second run (01M7MN3A73WF65M7ZPNMQJGCJV).
